meta.title: Move Firefox Bookmarks to Chrome | Snug
meta.description: Export Firefox bookmarks to an HTML file and import it into Chrome, step by step, with what to check afterwards. Menu paths verified {date}.

title: How do I move my bookmarks from Firefox to Chrome?
directAnswer: Export your bookmarks from Firefox to an HTML file with {fromExportPath}. Then import that file into Chrome with {toImportPath}. Chrome puts them in {toImportPlacement}. Menu paths checked {date}.

builtIn.title: The built-in method
builtIn.intro: Both browsers do this on their own. You need the HTML file and nothing else.
steps: Save the file. Firefox names it {fromExportFile} by default.
Choose the HTML file you saved and confirm.

carriesOver.title: What carries over
carriesOver.intro: The HTML file is the only thing that moves.
items: Left out of the file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlDrops}.
Where a help page does not say, this page says Not listed instead of guessing.

withSnug.title: With Snug
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome and other Chromium browsers, not in Firefox. Export the HTML file from Firefox as above, then use Snug in Chrome for the import. It adds a preview, a choice of what to bring in and a way back.
steps: Install Snug from the Chrome Web Store.
Open Snug's Import page and choose the HTML file there, or drop it on the page. Do not use the popup for this: it imports at once, without a preview.
The Preview shows the detected format, the bookmark count and the folder tree before anything changes.
Use the checkboxes to pick single bookmarks or whole folders. Snug imports only what you select.

Choose an import mode. Create folder adds everything to a new Imported Bookmarks folder. Restore — merge places bookmarks in their original locations next to your existing ones, when the file carries them.
Leave Skip duplicates on. It leaves out any bookmark whose address is already in Chrome, and tells you how many it skipped.
withSnug.snapshot: Create folder and Restore — merge never clear your bookmarks. Before a Restore — replace, Snug saves a Safety snapshot to your Downloads and keeps a copy in Settings, so you can undo the import.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: You cannot find the bookmarks after importing. Chrome places them in {toImportPlacement}.
Chrome does not accept the file. Check that you chose the HTML file Firefox saved, named {fromExportFile} by default, and not another file type.
A bookmark appears twice. Open Duplicates in Snug: it groups copies by address and removes only the copies you mark Delete.
Snug says nothing was imported. Every bookmark in the file is already in your browser. Turn off Skip duplicates to import them again.

verified: Menu paths and file names were read from the official help pages of {fromName} and {toName} on {date}. Browser menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen.
